race_context: The Metropolitan School District (MSD) of New Durham Township runs Westville Schools in Westville, LaPorte County {msdnd_home}. Westville Middle/High School serves grades 7-12 and had 427 students in 2023-24, according to Wikipedia; a district-wide enrollment figure was not found {wiki_whs}. Superintendent: Brian Ton {msdnd_home}{msdnd_min_20260114}.

The board is an elected five-member Board of School Trustees serving four-year terms, with three or two seats up every two years, according to the district {msdnd_board}. Current members listed by the district: Mark Parkman (president), Karen Jedrysek (vice president), Lynn Wilson (secretary), Phil Burdine (deputy secretary) and Wayne Hodge (member) {msdnd_board}. In January 2026 the board moved its regular meetings to the third Wednesday of each month at 6 p.m. {msdnd_reorg_2026}.

Past elections: in 2020 and 2024 the county ballot carried one district-wide at-large race electing two members (Karen Jedrysek alone in 2020; Philip Burdine and Karen Jedrysek, the only two candidates, in 2024) {lpc_2020}{lpc_2024}. In 2022 the only MSD race on ballots in the New Durham 01, New Durham 02 and Westville precincts was 'Metropolitan Sch Dist - New Durham At Lg', vote for one, between Wayne R. Hodge and Mark Parkman; Parkman led in all three precinct reports reviewed {lpc_2022_nd01}{lpc_2022_nd02}{lpc_2022_wv}.

Seats on the 2026 ballot (state list): 'Metropolitan School Board of New Durham' (Mark D. Parkman vs. Wayne R. Hodge), 'Metropolitan School Board, Northeast' (Matt Driscoll, unopposed) and 'Metropolitan School Board, Northwest' (Jeff D. Porter, unopposed), each vote for one {in_list}. Parkman and Hodge both sit on the current board, so the New Durham race is between two sitting members {msdnd_board}{in_list}. Neither Driscoll nor Porter is a current member {msdnd_board}.

Seat count and naming: three seats on the 2026 ballot matches the district's description of three or two seats per cycle {msdnd_board}. However, the Northeast and Northwest seats did not appear on 2022 county ballots, and the state list gives no county for those two offices, so it could not be confirmed that they belong to the MSD of New Durham Township or which current members, if any, hold them {in_list}{lpc_2022_nd01}{lpc_2022_wv}.
Party labels: Parkman and Hodge are listed as Nonpartisan and Driscoll and Porter as Republican on the state list; 2026 is the first year Indiana school board candidates could list a party {in_list}.

Building project and bonds (July–Oct. 2026): the board held a first preliminary determination hearing for a building project on July 22, 2026, when a resident asked about the nature of the projects; on July 28 it adopted the project, preliminary determination and reimbursement resolutions {msdnd_min_20260722}{msdnd_min_20260728}. The district's school building corporation and board scheduled Oct. 14, 2026 votes on a seventh amendment to the corporation's lease and on the issuance of bonds {msdnd_bc_20261014}{msdnd_ag_20261014}. The posted documents do not give the project's cost or scope.

Budget: a public hearing on the 2027 budget, capital projects plan and bus replacement plan was set for Sept. 30, 2026, with adoption of the 2027 budget on the Oct. 14, 2026 agenda {msdnd_ag_20260930}{msdnd_ag_20261014}. The district is not among those that filed for a November 2026 property tax referendum {dlgf_ref}.

Other 2025-26 board business: a 2025-2027 tentative agreement and master contract with the Westville Teachers Association (October–November 2025) {msdnd_ag_20251029}{msdnd_ag_20251113}; the student transfer policy and capacity for 2026-27 (April 2026) {msdnd_ag_20260415}; the superintendent's January 2026 briefing on state legislation including bell-to-bell student cell phone limits {msdnd_min_20260114}; regular updates on the district's solar installation {msdnd_min_20260722}; and an Oct. 14, 2026 resolution on employee pay for emergency school closures in August 2026 {msdnd_ag_20261014}.

No candidate forum, questionnaire or news coverage of this race was found, and none of the four candidates has a campaign committee on LaPorte County's 2026 campaign finance report list {lpc_finance}. Board agendas and minutes are posted on the district site {msdnd_agendas}.
